item.title: Gnome tree (repost)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Festive/ Horror

Page Layout (Optional):

Elevator Pitch: The Gnome Tree Is a Classic Christmas tree, but with a twist, Sometimes, there are Animate Small, limbless Scandinavian Christmas Gnomes, such as dolls and ornaments, while outside of the tree, these gnomes are quite mischievous, sometimes when the tree ejects non anomalous Christmas Decorations, and these gnomes will attempt to ‘Decorate’ the containment cell, along with covering up CCTV footage

Central Narrative: These Gnomes Have a Rigid Hierarchy, where each different Gnome does it’s designed task, The Lowest in the hierarchy, The Gnome Guards, can do very simple tasks, as long as there is a group of three or more or them, these Guards are so Basic, that they have been known to accept orders from almost any life form, including humans, making it possible for testing with the object

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The tree is actually a portal to a Subterranean Festively decorated village. Where countless numbers of these gnomes reside, on a Exploration into the village with a D-Class, the live body cam footage shown gnomes never seen before, like the leader of this village, when the D-Class if found, hundreds of Gnomes Gather around him, and then made Syncretized attack, body footage cuts off for only a few disturbing images to be shown, after the footage comes back on, it shows two guard gnomes studying what the camera is, body footage cuts off again only to show A Tied up D-Class carried on his back into a large Factory located on the right side of the village, where gnomes were shown to put materials such as wool and cotton though the one side, and a dozen gnomes come out of the other side, after the D-Class was fully inside of the Factory, on the other side An Entire Army of Lower Hierarchy Gnomes, along with some High Hierarchy Gnomes

item.title: SCP Idea: Pinular Gas
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): I don't really know how I would put this, so if you want to see the sandbox page just ask.

Elevator Pitch:
There's a gas that when inhaled causes negative affects on the victim.
*This gas slowly turns the victims into Wood.
*If the wood corpse of the victim has a piece remove, the piece removed will melt into a pile of skin-like material and blood that is classified as SCP-XXXX-2
*If the victim is taken to the desired area they have after inhalation, they will be free of the negative affects and mutate into SCP-XXXX-3.

Central Narrative: None at the moment, may have a new instance in the future.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The reason for this to stick out or to make it popular is for the following reasons:

  • It may be the first SCP to be a gas that upon inhalation begins a transformation process
  • After inhalation, the situation becomes life or death, as the subject must be transported to their desired location to survive.

Additional Notes: The last time I had posted, it ended up reaching -14 ratings, and that made me very disappointed in myself, so my goal is to make my SCP more likable.
Another goal of mine is to get some help with any grammar mess-ups on my article, as well as making the article's input more eloquent.

item.title: Super Mario Syndicate
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Media/Satire/Surrealism

Elevator Pitch: A ROM hack of Super Mario World in which every Mario and Luigi who ever died form a union, the levels are the offices of major videogame companies and the sites of riots where police brutality occurred.

Central Narrative: Millions of Marios and Luigis live in a union building, where they raise all the Baby Marios lost in Yoshi's Island. Play of the game has been tied to various spinal compression industries in videogame executives which led to the discovery and tracking of the anomalous ROM. In the wake of various Riots, new "Lost Levels" are encountered where the player can jump on the heads of police officers. This leads to the liquidation of an entire police precinct in an undisclosed US city. The Foundation has trained speed-runners in the Media Department who can play through as pacifists to safely explore. A sub-faction, Luigi's For Ethical Treatment of Yoshi's (LFETY), is discovered, and horribly executes Mario's with dual-Yoshi-bisection (similar to horse quartering) who have performed the Yoshi Sacrifice to complete Star Road. The bisected Mario's are still alive, those who have used a Fire Flower can burn themselves to death.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Everyone's favorite videogame meets political violence.

Additional Notes: Early draft is done, could use more fleshing out but I like the idea of a fairly concise Media SCP that evokes a concept without having to do elaborated logs and progression/reclassification narrative. Someone made a Communist Mario 3 ROM with a great image to headline with attribution.

item.title: Kendall Jenner Pepsi Ad
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Media/Satire/Infiltration

Elevator Pitch: An anomalous version of the infamous Kendall Jenner Pepsi ad that iterates until it begins depicting the Foundation as the police and begins detailing containment procedures.

Central Narrative: DOGM OVIE format, we iterate through increasingly lurid, then occult iterations of the Pepsi ad, the artist, journalist, nature of the protest and police counter-measures, as well as the behavior of the Pepsi drinking officer, all change progressive until things becoming chillingly specific. All testing is ceased, an analyst from the Media Department who has watched the video 5000 times is put through a Loyalty Test, deemed non-compromised, left under surveillance. Some time later the SCP is reclassified to Euclid from Safe when a secondary -A effect is discovered where each playback has cast a sort of radiation, which has collided with several other SCPs and empowered them.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The thematically most vile, yet nihilistic, piece of media ever produced as a virulent media SCP, possible Chaos Insurgency attempt at infiltration.

Additional Notes: Already drafted, mostly formatted (need help with the wiki-table format), ~2.4k words. Playback descriptions follow format of:

item.title: Forum Crit Team - Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

item.title: Re: Freddy's Fishman (seeking Greenlight & Critique)
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there Dr Elliot Anemone. Apologies for the delay in getting this critique to you. Let’s take a look at your concept.

+ crit
- crit

While the idea sounds interesting, and the new, proposed GoI has potential, I feel your Central Narrative has a couple of convenient conjectures that don’t really hold up to scrutiny. I’ll list a couple below for you to iron out:

after something interfered with the communications between the foundation and the agents

What interfered with the communications? Is this crucial to the story, or simply a way for you (the author) to get the MTF captured? Speaking of being captured, what happens to the MTF? You quickly go into another set of Foundation agents who discover the scp – why not simply start your discovery log at this point? Was there a need for the MTF to go in first?

Doctor Josef Monstrosity thanking the foundation for finding their med students projects, and left this one as a show of thanks.

Why would this gesture be “a show of thanks”?

attempts by the Foundation to gain the Fishmans trust in hopes that it is capable of telling the Foundation where it came from

If it were experimented on by the medical students, wouldn’t the Fishman automatically side with the Foundation? Why the resistance to give up a place and people who tortured it?

Dr. Franklin, a young researcher with vague origins, but was brought in by the higher ups so staff just decide it's best not to question it

Again, this sounds dubious at best, unprofessional at worst. You’ve introduced a character to advance the story, and nothing else. There’s no reason for his inclusion at this point unless you have a good explanation for his appearance.

how it went to the hospital willingly at first because when it was human it had aquagenic urticaria and the hospital said they could cure him

This is a good motivation for the scip to have, and an excellent introduction to what the new GoI is capable / not capable of doing. The problem is you seem to have given us conflicting views of what the GoI actually is: is it a place for so-called monsters to go to get cured or experimented on?

how the Hospital views normalcy as an illness that needs to be remedied.

This, then, becomes even more problematic as you have an additional goal for the GoI. Why was it experimenting on the fish-man then? Wouldn’t it view all mutants as normal people?

Lots of plot inconsistencies I hope you can help clear up. If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll do my best to take another look. For now, all the best!


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: Freddy's Fishman (seeking Greenlight & Critique)

item.title: Re: "The Brain Game" a rough pitch
item.content:encoded:
On further consideration, you should consider how on-site soldiers are pawns, researchers are rooks, some perhaps humanoid Thaumiels on site are like Knights, some powerful tech or Thaumiel objects are rooks, the site director is the king and the lead researcher on this SCP is the Queen. Characterize some of these. Then on the SCP's side, it's the King, a Keter it makes a deal with to engineer a breach is the queen, lesser SCPs are the rest, and it's a chess game.

Or, mechanisms around site locks/sub-systems that the SCP compromises. Perhaps a mix.

Another key criticism you'll face is, how is this not just a non-anomalous AI. 079 seems more anomalous because it's an advanced AI from the 70s, and it was early series. You'll need to emphasize the preternatural jump in capability of the, presumably very basic Chess-expert algo, which shouldn't have any means to bootstrap general intelligence.

Just some quick sauce from my perusal, I'd greenlight the draft if I had the power.

Hi there Drewie. Apologies for the long delay in responding. Let’s take a look at your concept.

So there are a couple of common issues I’m seeing with the concept, which I’ll lay them out for you to work on:

(1) Your scp boils down to “a thing that does a thing.” In this case, they’re seeds that make you smart, and then kill you, for no apparent reason. Notice you haven’t given us a context, explanation or reason why these things happen, who made the seeds or why they were located in Iraq, for example. Are they tied to a specific GoI or entity? If so, what are their goals? Why does it create the effects you’ve described?

(2) Your ideas listed under a central narrative are in fact, a combination of multiple, smaller narratives. Notice you’ve listed a few ideas like testing logs, discovery logs, researcher logs etc., but haven’t given us specific details. Rather than simply summarise what you want to include in your article, actually tell us what the story is. Who found the original seeds? Who is the main researcher? How does the Foundation contain them?

item.title: Re: On the Shores of Paradise
item.content:encoded:
Hey there again, thanks for the recrit!
You bring up a good point, so here is my (quite long, admittedly. Sorry about the wall of text!) response:

+ Open Response +
Woooooooosh

So you tell me here that the whole thing feels a bit contrived for your liking (with the whole disaster thing and the gateway being a false solution):

I think the disaster that forces the Foundation to shove people into an idyllic pocket dimension feels contrived. It feels like there needed to be a reason to shove people in there, so a disaster scenario was thought up to put them on there.

Looking back on it, the concept does come off as a little bit… forced. However, you also provide a possible solution:

What if these 'disasters' were pre-constructed by the paradise land itself to entice people to come in and people walks right into the trap, hook, line, and sinker?

Interesting. I've thought about this for a while, and I might have just the thing for that.

I established that there are native flora and fauna in and around Paradise (both the shores and the actual pocket dimension), and that they are all universally docile. But what if the Foundation has underestimated them?

It starts off with the spirit (I know you're unimpressed by the spirit, but I haven't thought of a replacement yet) creating a couple of large, strong animals capable of breaching containment (as a placeholder, think something like a rhino) that are still quite docile. The Foundation finds these, almost has a containment breach or two, logs them, and is now wary. But then no more appear, and the Foundation relaxes.

This isn't the end though. A much more devious and subtle way of breaching containment comes in the form of small, parasitic, plant organisms that possess a powerful anomalous hallucinogen that can completely alter what a person sees. They are quite weak at first, and their stores of hallucinogen only last three days before they run out and die. However, they breed quickly, and they rapidly infest everyone on the local containment Site before setting up a large nest (no one can see it because they are all under the influence of the hallucinogen) to keep everyone permanently infested. Arriving personnel succumb as well, but they're only temporarily infested (just to make sure they don't see anything).

+ Open Response II: Electric Boogaloo +
This is the narrative

Anyway, both the protagonists are present on the Site (and thus infested) when they both see an email from the 05 Council notifying them of multiple catastrophic Keter-class containment breaches, and notifies them that communications will be down for the foreseeable future. The email tells them to evacuate as many civilians as possible by any method.

They both announce this to the Site through a memo, and discussions abound. Someone comes up with the idea to use the Paradise gateway to evacuate the civilians, and the argument between the two protagonists begins. Big ethical discussions (through emails and the like) and the protagonists have a falling-out. The protagonist who doesn't want to use the gateway (PrA) has flashes of the Site overrun by plants (initially dismissed as stress, but actually caused by a partial immunity to the hallucinogen), and instead of going away, the flashes become more frequent. This causes PrA to become incredibly suspicious, yet when they try to convince their friend (PrB), their claims are once again dismissed.

When both PrA and PrB see dark clouds on the horizon (both metaphorically and literally) tensions rise tremendously, and as PrA desperately tries to convince PrB that there is something wrong about all of this, PrB and the rest of the Site unintentionally gaslight PrA and convince them that they are suffering from prolonged stress, and tell them to have a rest (or something like that).

Soon after, PrB announces to the population near the beach the Foundation's existence and how they've failed their job, and that everyone needs to come with them if they want to live. There's mass panic obviously, but everyone is rallied together (meanwhile, the [hallucinated] dark clouds on the horizon are getting closer). PrA meets PrB on the beach after they've evacuated everyone (population is about ~95000) and the stuff in the 'Big Reveal' section above happens (except that PrA escapes instead of dying).

After this has been documented, there is an updated version of the file that appears, along with all the changes that have occurred to the anomaly.


To sum up, the Paradise used small organisms loaded with hallucinogenic toxins to overtake the Site overlooking it and manipulate everyone into thinking the world was ending, when in fact it wasn't, thus causing them to evacuate everyone into the gateway. This way, there is still ethical friction between the protagonists, but hopefully it isn't contrived as the other disaster.

TL;DR - Trippy plants from another dimension play the Foundation like a piano.

Anyway thanks for reading, and I hope this response suffices!

item.title: "The Brain Game" a rough pitch
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional

Elevator Pitch: The Brain Game starts out as a simple chess program, but over time it begins to communicated, learn, and develop a personality.

Central Narrative: The Brain Game interacts with it's researcher, Dr Hext, and eventually grows and learns, much like a child learns from a parent. Eventually it reaches self-awareness, and chose a name, Kaspar, derived from chess champion Garry Kasparov. However, it starts to desire to escape from the computer it is contained in. Kaspar/The Brain Game separates his consciousness from the chess program and escapes confinement in a robotic body. Whilst the foundation tracks him down, Dr Hext continues to experiment with the program, and finds that it starts to develop a new, entirely separate personality, and much faster too. The foundation manages to find Kaspar/The Brain Game, and manages to re-contain it. When re-contained, it refuses to talk to anyone but Dr Hext. Dr Hext talks to Kaspar, and tells him of the new personality, who has chosen the name "Magnus". Kaspar is overjoyed that he is no longer alone, and agrees to become Dr Hext's research assistant, and help Magnus learn and grow. Eventually Dr Hext dies, and Kaspar takes on a new name, Kaspar Hext, and continues to work for the foundation, alongside his brother Magnus.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Chess has always been seen as a gauge of intelligence and strategy, however Chess programs tend to be quite specialised for the purpose, and not good at anything else. However, the though occurred to me, what if someone created a chess program that learned to play chess the same way humans learn? What else would it learn? How would it react?

Additional Notes: I may split this into a article and a tale that goes into more depth. Feedback would be appreciated!

Forum thread: "The Brain Game" a rough pitch

item.title: The “normal” dude.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: Tale

Genre: Emotional, Comedy, Action

Elevator Pitch: A SCP writer (probably from our world) suddenly materialises in a SCP site. He swaps places with his other self (who is a clearance 2 junior researcher). Will he go on and reveal his true identity or live his dream life?

Central Narrative: The story begins with the writer doing living his boring life. We get an insight with his relations with the SCP writing community. The writer then goes up to his computer (to write stuff) then walks out his room, but instead of walking out into the living room, he walks into a testing chamber. The Foundation staff casually greet him and tell him to continue the experiment. Then we get a deeper insight into his life with the him thinking about blending himself in with the scp Foundation, or revealing his identity. He chooses to blend in, and the rest of the tale is him trying to blend in with some comedy elements.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Well overall I think the idea of a all knowing scp writer suddenly appearing in the universe he wrote is quite interesting.

Additional Notes: I can always make this into an scp if you guys want.

So, there isn't a whole lot going on here, narrative or otherwise. It's a cave with strong gravity that gets stronger as you go in.

So what?

There is nothing presented here for readers to get invested with, nor is there much to work with in the way of narrative tension. Explain to us why we should care about this cave. Mayve it's harbouring some dark secrets. Maybe it holds the key to why Wikidot breaks every other day. These are obviously not good examples, but you must give us something otherwise you'll never captivate the reader's attention.

item.title: Re: Please green light me
item.content:encoded:
Marcelles D. Raynes at your service, I'll take a look at this post.

Let's dive in, shall we?
Close

There's a couple things here that drew my attention, and I am going to address them in no particular order.

It would have a Keter level containment procedures on par with 682

While I understand that you want to attempt to convey the scope of your anomaly, comparing it to a well known, albeit poorly written, article is going to raise the bar of scrutiny from reviewers immediately. I don't see how a plastic, shapeshifting car warrants containment measures of this magnitude. In reality the Foundation would just lock it in a box and forget about it.

and no one would know what it is because it's redacted.

Redacting containment procedures is nevet a good way to go. In-universe the con procs are there to ensure the greatest chance of containment of any given anomaly, and to save people's lives should said anomaly escape. However, if you're referring to us not knowing what the anomaly is, I would not recommend this either. There are ways to make redactions work though.

The story here is non-existent. All we are given to work with is, quite honestly, a very boring anomaly with rudimentary abilities and no narrative to become invested in. There are ways to make narratives work, even with simple anomalies, but they are often more focused on characters or environmental beats. I would suggest reading up on some newly released SCPs for narrative inspiration.

That's all I've got for you. Good luck.

I find myself agreeing with a lot of the DV's on here. There's not a lot of substance to this other than "cartoon tropes happening in real life" and there doesn't really seem to be much else.

As someone who is writing a "cartoon trope happening in real life" SCP right now, I think this misses one of the most important steps when writing one of these, and that's twisting and realizing the ideas shown here.

I feel it would have been a lot more interesting if this article where to have gone into detail as to how this would affect Researcher Rex in the long run. I can imagine that having to go through 100 tests of bizarre and insane cartoon logic would definitely take somewhat of a mental toll on a person.

This is charming, but I will sadly have to -1 for these reasons.

item.title: Re: Please green light me
item.content:encoded:
Yeah, I really just don't see the appeal here. I'll try to do my best conveying the problems I have with this and some possible solutions on how to fix this up.

+ show block
– hide block

A sentient toy car that can change based on its mood.

Sentient shapeshifting toys have already been done before and have been done so more effectively. So have shapeshifters that change when they get mood swings.

The special containment procedures change based on its toy. For example, one is a toy plane and another is a lego figure. People would have to change its cell or move it to a new cell when this happens.

This is not a central narrative, this is something that should have been told to us in the elevator pitch, it doesn't tell us anything about the main story beats or if there even is a story here, and you don't tell us if you wanna convey a theme here instead of a narrative. You also never provided context as to why the Foundation would have to transfer the anomaly through cells, does the anomaly's size change significantly or produce certain anomalous effects that actively damage the containment chamber every time it changes? What do you mean by "People would have to change its cell.."? Containment cells aren't readily available on the get-go for any anomaly that needs moving around, which there's a lot that do.

The special containment procedures for each "version." One type of toy for its mood, anger, would be redacted. It would have a Keter level containment procedures on par with 682 and no one would know what it is because it's redacted.

I don't really see how this is a hook, it's just telling us why and how the containment procedures would be tricky depending on its moods, not telling us why anyone should be interested in this. Why would the anger stage be redacted? Wouldn't it make more sense in-universe if what happens when the anomaly is angry not be redacted at all? Think about it you're a researcher studying this thing and you barely have any info on it besides that it's some weird shapeshifting thing that has emotions, and that their behavior and anomalous traits are directly affected by these emotions. You would wanna know what happens when certain circumstances are met and what it could pose for its containment and all future handling, keep in mind SCP documents are read by other researchers in-universe too, so you would wanna let them know what happens too. They don't just sit around in the Foundation archives and databases.

"It would have a Keter level containment procedures on par with 682 and no one would know what it is because it's redacted.", this sentence makes 0 sense. No one would know what this KETER LEVEL THREAT'S containment procedures would because they're all redacted? Why would the Foundation allow this to happen..ever?? How would other Foundation personnel even handle this thing's containment, even if they could? That crucial piece of information would be cut-off from them entirely, and you legit just described to us the containment procedures and that there would be a lot of them in the article…

Why would 682's and this random anomaly's containment procedures be on par with each other? Just because they're Keter? Every Keter's (and almost every) anomaly's containment procedures are different in one way or capacity. Just seems like a useless bit of 'info' you threw out there that still doesn't tell anyone why they should be interested in this thing.

You do know most of this stuff should have gone into the elevator pitch as well, right?

Like I said above, I feel like this concept is generally uninteresting, everything you're trying to go for with this has already been done better by other writers, multiple times, and you're not really adding a new spin on this or giving narrative substance to make up for it. I suggest playing around with the shapeshifting part of the anomaly, experiment a bit, and bring something new to the table by utilizing the shape-shifting concept or completely shapeshifting the ideas of shapeshifting itself (ahaha get it, haha-hah, you do get it right…? I'm so sorry for subjecting you to these horrible puns). If it's sentient and it's anomalous abilities directly derive from its emotions then you should try to imagine what emotion would look like in a physical form, through this anomaly's shape-shifting. Or you could make a narrative by focusing on the anomaly's feelings and it's point of view, explore why it feels this way and why it's like this in the first place, is it a curse, a toy made to be played with, or just an oddity like all the others? These are just ideas I'm throwing out here. Best of luck with this concept!
